decisions.rationale: Peer-fix re-review: 36 observed months, 5.24 mph vs a 6.66 mph median of 32-33 Manhattan local peers (route_family_type method in every month, zero fallback). Average deficit 1.43 mph (~21% below the matched median), and the per-month deficit never drops below 1.20 mph - above the 1 mph floor in all 36 months. Large in relative terms, fully stable, and the borough+class peer group is defensible; the claim text now names the method ('median of 32 same-class peer routes'). Publishable as a matched-peer ranking statement.
decisions.notes: Batch-1 label was route_context solely because every month used the dishonest system-wide fallback pool (~327 routes, 8.83 mph inflated median, recorded deficit 3.60). The 2026-06-11 class-based peer fix replaced that with same-borough locals; the honest deficit is smaller (1.43 mph) but holds in 100% of months against a like-for-like group, which removes the only blocker. Descriptive comparison, not a causal control.

The largest same-borough local pool in the batch, fully stable deficit, claim text names the method. Publishable as a matched-peer ranking statement.
decisions.notes: Batch-1 label was route_context because all 36 months used the system-wide fallback (~327 routes, 8.83 median, recorded deficit 2.87). The class-based fix compares BX2 against same-borough locals; the deficit narrows to 1.49 mph but is the most stable in the batch (min 1.33). Descriptive comparison, not a causal control.

decisions.rationale: Peer-fix re-review: 36 observed months, 5.63 mph vs the 6.66 mph median of 32-33 Manhattan local peers (route_family_type in every month). Average deficit is only 1.03 mph - barely above the detector's 1 mph floor - and the per-month deficit (0.91-1.23 mph) clears the floor in just 17 of 36 months. The peer group is now honest, but the gap is small and not month-by-month stable, so a ranking/superlative claim would overstate it. Stays context on magnitude, not methodology.
decisions.notes: Batch-1 label was route_context because of the system-wide fallback pool (deficit then read 3.20 vs the inflated 8.83 median). The blocker is resolved, but against the honest M-local median the deficit shrinks to ~1 mph and is near-threshold, so the label stays route_context for a different (magnitude) reason.

decisions.rationale: Peer-fix re-review: 36 observed months, 5.60 mph vs the 6.66 mph median of 32-33 Manhattan local peers (route_family_type in every month). Average deficit 1.06 mph, per-month range 0.63-1.35 mph, above the 1 mph floor in only 23 of 36 months - the least stable surviving local (minimum deficit 0.63 mph is well under the floor). Honest peer group, but the gap is small and unstable; not publishable as a ranking. Stays context on magnitude/stability.
decisions.notes: Batch-1 label was route_context because of the system-wide fallback pool (deficit then read 3.23 vs the inflated 8.83 median). Against the honest M-local median the deficit shrinks to ~1.1 mph with the widest per-month spread of the four locals, so the label stays route_context for a magnitude/stability reason rather than peer-group dishonesty.

decisions.rationale: Peer-fix re-review: 36 observed months, 5.75 mph vs the 8.77 mph median of the 19-route citywide SBS pool (route_type method in every month - class-only, no borough/spatial match). Average deficit 3.02 mph, per-month range 2.37-3.67 mph, above the floor in all 36 months: large and stable. But the SBS pool mixes boroughs and corridor types (long-arterial SBS with wide stop spacing vs a dense Manhattan crosstown), so 'slowest SBS' partly measures corridor geometry, not route performance; detector confidence is itself low. Upgradable to honest descriptive context now that the claim names the 19-route class pool, but not to a primary ranking against this pool.
decisions.notes: Batch-1 label was needs_more_evidence because the SBS route was ranked against the system-wide local+express pool - the sharpest mismatch in the batch. That evidence gap is closed: the comparison is now SBS-vs-SBS with the method recorded per month, which is enough for route_context. The remaining ceiling is the pool itself: 19 heterogeneous citywide SBS routes (route_type fallback, not route_family_type) with off-route structural confounds.

decisions.rationale: Peer-fix re-review: 36 observed months, 5.94 mph vs the 8.77 mph median of the 19-route citywide SBS pool (route_type method in every month). Average deficit 2.83 mph, per-month range 2.21-3.29 mph, above the floor in all 36 months: large and stable. Same structural caveat as M34+: the class-only SBS pool spans boroughs and corridor geometries, so the deficit conflates crosstown-corridor geometry with route performance, and detector confidence is low. Honest descriptive context against a named 19-route class pool; not a publishable primary ranking.
decisions.notes: Batch-1 label was needs_more_evidence because of the SBS-vs-system-pool mismatch. The class-based fix closes that gap (SBS-vs-SBS, method named in the claim), supporting an upgrade to route_context, but the small heterogeneous route_type pool keeps it short of primary_finding.
